papers.q: Describe briefly on Vit.D metabolism, clinical features and management of Vit.D deficiency? [5+3+2]

A 30-year-old lady came to you with fever of 3 days, decreased food intake and nausea. Clinically jaundice was present. There were similar cases in the family. What is the clinical diagnosis? What are the differential diagnoses? How will you proceed to evaluate? How do you prevent the condition. [2+2+3+3]

Mention the causes for chronic aches and pains. How do you differentiate that from inflammatory arthritis? How do you evaluate a patient with chronic aches and pains? Describe briefly regarding management of chronic pain? [2+2+2+4]
Enumerate the causes of falls in the elderly. How would you assess the risks of fall in elderly? How can we prevent falls in elderly? [4+3+3]
A 45-year-old overweight man came to you with recent onset tiredness, dryness of mouth, weight loss and nocturia. What is your clinical diagnosis? How will you manage him after diagnosis? [10]
Describe the condition and causes of gastroesophageal reflux diseases (GERD), give anatomical basis of GERD? Write briefly on the management of GERD from a family medicine perspective? [4+3+3]
Enumerate skin, mucosal, and systemic manifestations of protein calorie malnutrition. [4+3+3]
What is delirium? How is it different from dementia? Enumerate the causes, differential diagnosis and management of delirium? [1+1+3+3+2]
Write briefly on reasons for chemical poisonings. Enumerate clinical features, management, and complications of organophosphorus poisoning? [3+3+2+2]

A 50 year old male known to have diabetes and hypertension for 15 years. He had history of acute coronary syndrome a year ago. Now comes to you with fatigue, decreased food intake and dyspnea on exertion. Clinically pedal edema, elevated JVP and on bilateral auscultation of the lung bases, he had fine crepitations. What clinical possibilities will you entertain? How do you proceed to evaluate this patient? As a family physician, how will you manage this case? [2+4+4]

A 38-year-old Mr. Ravi was brought to the casualty with the history of first episode of seizures lasting for one minute. There was up rolling of eyes and drooling of saliva with loss of consciousness, regained consciousness after 2 minutes. There was no post ictal phase. The entire episode lasted for 5 min. Wife of Mr. Ravi gives history of alcohol intake by him of 180ml for past 20 years. His last drink was 3 days back – since he didn’t have work and didn’t have money. His BP is 130/80, PR- 92/min, SpO2- 100 %, GRBS- 110, He is oriented to time, place, person. a) What is your differential diagnosis? [2] b) What is your approach for above mentioned scenario? [5] c) If GRBS- 50mg%. How will you treat immediately? [1] d) How will you manage Alcohol related complications? [2]

Mrs. Pratibha 73-years-old, staying with her spouse presents to Outpatient department with history of fall 2 days back in her home. Six months ago also, she had a similar complaint and she sustained a Colle’s fracture of the right hand. Her first fall was one year ago when she sustained minor abrasions. a) What is the pathophysiology of Falls? [2] b) What are the risk factors? [2] c) How will you do the OPD assessment of falls? [4] d) How are you going to prevent further falls in Mrs. Pratibha? [2]

A 23-year-old man was admitted to emergency room of primary care hospital for vomiting and upper abdominal pain. His random blood sugar was found to be 586mg/dl. He is hemodynamically stable. His urine ketones were +++ a) Mention the immediate life-threatening condition this patient can have. [1] b) Mention the investigations you would want to do, substantiate you answer. [3] c) What are the complications of this condition? [2] d) Discuss the management of this condition in detail up to discharge. [4]

A 67-year-old lady was brought to the emergency room with h/o dizziness but no loss of consciousness. She is a known diabetic and hypertensive, occasionally noncompliant with her medications. Her BP is 130/86mmHg, PR- 86/min - irregularly irregular, GRBS- 186mg%. a) What immediate office investigation would you do? [1] b) What may be the most probable diagnosis? [1] c) What other investigations you would want to do? [2] d) What are the complications of this condition? [2] e) How will you assess this patient for stroke risk? [2] f) How will you manage this patient? [2]

A 40-year-old lady presented to outpatient department with multiple joint pain, hair loss, oral ulcers, malar rash, breathlessness, and history of passing blood in urine. a) How will you evaluate the history and physical finding to come to a woking diagnosis in an adult patient with multiple inflammatory arthritis? [4] b) What are your differential diagnosis? [2] c) What investigations you would want to do? [2] d) What are the complications of the most probable diagnosis? [2]

A 48-year-old lady, known case of diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, presented to outpatient department with skin lesions over her elbows, knee, which has increased over past 3 weeks. Earlier she had small lesion for which she used moisturizer which didn’t bother her much. These lesions are well defined, erythematous plaques, with irregular borders and silvery scales. a) What is the most probable final diagnosis? And how will you confirm your diagnosis? [2] b) How will you manage this condition? [4] c) What are the complications of this condition? [3] d) When will you refer this patient to a specialist? [1]

A 48-year-old Mrs.Lata has been diagnosed with end stage Breast cancer and her oncologist told her that there is no further treatment. She wants to discuss with you about her feelings and about the events which may follow: a) End of life care. [5] b) Advanced directives.in the light of indian laws and guidelines. [5]

A 42-year-old Ravi was working in fields when he suddenly had snake bite. Before he or his fellow workers could identify, the snake had escaped. a) Which are the common snake bites in India? [1] b) From the clinical features of the patient, how would you identify the type of snake bite? [2] c) What investigations will you do (bed side and Lab)? [2] d) What are the complications of snake bite? [2] e) How will you treat Snake envenomation? [3]

A 48-year-old Krishnan presented to OPD with history of Abdominal distension over past 3 weeks, gradually increasing, His wife gives history that he was diagnosed as a case of cirrhosis of liver 6 months ago: a) What are the common causes of cirrhosis? [2] b) What are the clinical manifestations - symptoms and signs of cirrhosis? [2] c) What are the complications of cirrhosis? [2] d) How will you manage (INV+Treatment) this patient? [2] e) How will you assess the severity of cirrhosis? [2]

A 45-year-old woman - P3L3 - is accompanied by her daughter for episodes of fear and palpitations. She is a known hypertensive and is on telmisartan - thiazide 40/12.5mg OD. Since January, following a marital conflict, she has experienced multiple episodes of sudden onset of palpitations, sweating and dizziness. She is fearful of similar recurrence of such episodes. Her multiple visits to hospitals during those episodes showed a BP- 220/120 mmHg with negative cardiology work-up. Her vital signs now - BP- 160/90 mmHg, P-90/min, no elevated JVP or pedal oedema. a) Describe the diagnostic criteria of panic attacks. [3] b) List the possible medical conditions that may mimic a panic attack. [2] c) Describe the options of pharmacotherapy for this patient. [3] d) What are the non-pharmacological treatment options for this patient? [2]

Mr. A, is a 35 year old asthmatic on inhalers and regular follow up. He had no acute asthma attacks for the last 8 months. He developed sudden onset of breathlessness and was rushed to the hospital. a) How do you clinically assess him for severe asthma? [2] b) How will you manage acute asthma attack? [2] c) How will you prevent asthma exacerbation? [2] d) On examination, patient is found to have trachea deviated to the right side and absent air entry on the left side of the chest. What is the likely diagnosis and what are the other clinical features for this? [2] e) How will you manage this condition? [2]

Mrs. S had fever for 2 days. 5 days later, she developed severe pain in both the hands, fingers and toes. She has stiffness of hands and fingers in the mornings for about 45 minutes. She consults you after 1 week for her symptoms. a) What diagnosis will you entertain and what treatment will you provide? [2] Patient continues to have symptoms and there is no improvement even after 8 months. During the period, she has loss of hair and mouth ulcers. b) What differential diagnosis will you consider? [2] c) What investigations will you order? [3] d) Patient has been seen by a rheumatologist and started on Prednisolone and Methotrexate. He has asked you to monitor the patient. How will you do it? [3]

A 45-year-old man who has been drinking 3-4 pegs of whisky for few years, comes with complaints of yellowish discolouration of the eyes and loss of appetite along with abdomen pain. His last drink was 12 hrs ago. The family is worried and asks you to evaluate him and manage. a) What are the possible causes for his jaundice? [1] b) What tool can be used to screen for alcohol abuse? [2] c) What laboratory tests will confirm your diagnosis? [3] d) The patient is not willing to go to the hospital immediately and wants to wait for 2 to 3 days. What treatment will you provide before the patient decides to go to hospital? [2] e) Patient has been discharged from the hospital, how will you prevent a relapse of his alcohol problem? [2]

A patient who was diagnosed to be infected with HIV, has been started on cotrimoxazole as prophylaxis. Two days later, he develops ulcers in the mouth and diffuse rash all over the body. a) What is the differential diagnosis? [2] b) How will you treat this condition? [5] c) What are the infections he is at risk for? [3]

Mr. M is an obese individual. He was diagnosed as having diabetes and started on Tab. Glibenclamide 5mg two times a day. Three days after starting the treatment, his wife found that he was unresponsive and called you to see the patient. a) What is the likely diagnosis? [1] b) What treatment will you institute at home? [2] c) He is shifted to your nursing home. What treatment will you provide in the hospital? [3] d) What medication and advice will you provide on discharge? [4]

A 20-year-old lady presents with fever, headache and vomiting for the past 3 days. a) What is your differential diagnosis? [2] b) What clinical features will you elicit to assess her? [2] c) Outline the investigations and management of bacterial and tuberculous meningitis. [6]

Mr A. is a 70-year-old man who runs a small store. Recently his family has noticed that he has been very forgetful. His accounts in the shop has been going wrong. He has also started neglecting his personal grooming. At nights he shouts and says that he is seeing relatives who have died and are calling him. Sometimes he is incontinent of urine. a) What is the likely diagnosis? Outline the causes for it. [3] b) Discuss investigations that will help you assess for this conditon. [4] c) Discuss how you will help the patient and the family as their family doctor. [3]

A 70-year-old lady presents with pain of the left shoulder for the 2 weeks. She is a diabetic and a hypertensive. a) List the differential diagnosis. [2] b) You suspect that she could be having coronary heart disease. How will you investigate to confirm this? [3] c) Outline the management of effort angina and unstable angina. [5]

Mrs. Shakila, 30-year-old female, works as a clerk in Government office. She presented to your OPD with complaints of recurrent headache for the past 2 years, 3-4 episodes per month, associated with nausea and occasional vomiting, a) What could be the cause of her headache? How do you evaluate her? [3] b) How do you classify headaches? What are the common causes? [3] c) Mention 2 drugs that cause headache. [1] d) What are the red flags in history and physical examination of headaches? [3]

A 68-year-old male was brought to you with history of sudden onset headache and difficulty in using left upper and lower limbs since past 40 min. He was stuporous and BP- was190//120mmHg, Power in Left UL and LL was 2/5. a) What is your clinical diagnosis in this patient? Mention the causes of cerebrovascular accidents. [2] b) How do you clinically differentiate between thrombotic and hemorrhagic strokes? [3] c) What are the findings on CT for a hemorrhagic stroke? [2] d) What are the indications of thrombolysis and what are the guidelines for administration of r-tPA? [3]

A 58-years-old female presented to you with history of feeling hopelessness, tiredness for 3 months and has put on 5 kg weight, feels fatigued and drowsy: a) Which are the medical conditions that can mimic depression? [3] b) What are the criteria for a depressive episode? [3] c) What is the tool used as a diagnostic aid in primary care? [2] d) When do you refer a patient of depression to a specialist? [2]

A 56-year-old male presented to OPD with complaints of swelling of feet and breathing difficulty which has been increasing over the past 8 weeks. He is a diabetic and hypertensive: a) What are the precipitating causes of cardiac failure? [2] b) What are the signs of left and right heart failure? [2] c) What investigations you would want to perform? [2] d) What are the nonpharmacological and pharmacological managements? [4]

A 45-year-old male daily wage labourer has presented to you with recurrent episodes of breathlessness, cough and sputum production. He has given history of smoking since he was 15 years old, till recently he had been smoking 1 pack per day: a) How do you differentiate between bronchial asthma and COPD? [2] b) Write the differences on physical examination and chest X-ray, between obstructive and restrictive lung disease. [3] c) What are the complications of COPD? [2] d) Write briefly the management of COPD. [3]

Miss Renuka had eaten prawn fry brought from outside. Suddenly she started feeling itching all over body. She developed urticarial rashes. Her PR- 122, BP- 80/45mmHg and SpO2- 90%: a) What is the condition? How will you assess the patient? [3] b) What are the causes of her condition? [1] c) How will you manage her? [4] d) What advice will you give her to prevent it? [2]

A 74-year-old woman presents for her annual physical examination and notes increasing fatigue over the past 3 months. Her history is notable for longstanding systolic hypertension. A physical examination now demonstrates a blood pressure of 120/70 mmHg and an irregular pulse of approximately 120 bpm at rest. The patient’s body mass index is 22. An electrocardiogram confirms atrial fibrillation with a ventricular response of 120 bpm and ECG suggestive of left ventricular hypertrophy. An echocardiogram done a year earlier to evaluate left ventricular hypertrophy was notable only for mild, global left ventricular dysfunction with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% and mild mitral regurgitation. The patient’s chronic medical regimen includes lisinopril 20 mg, metoprolol XL 25 mg and 75 mg aspirin daily. A repeat echocardiogram performed in the office demonstrates an ejection fraction of 20% with global hypokinesis. a) What medications should be chosen to control the rate acutely? [2] b) What further work up is required for new onset AF? [2] c) Should one restore sinus rhythm or choose a strategy of rate control? [2] d) What are the anticoagulation requirements for this patient? [2] e) If the decision is made to maintain sinus rhythm after the cardioversion, what are the best medical or procedural options? [2]

A 29-year-old male has come with history of painless ulcer for the past 2 weeks over the penis. On examination, there is a single nontender indurated ulcer on the penis. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged: 2024 May paper 1 a) List the conditions which can cause genital ulcers. [2] b) What serological tests should be done? [2] c) How will you manage this patient? [2] 2 months later, he presents with urethral discharge. d) What organisms cause urethral discharge? [2] e) How will you manage him in this visit? [2]

A 30-year-old male presented to you with complaints of groin itching, which you diagnosed as fungal infection and you wanted to rule out diabetes and the GRBS- 297mg%: a) How do you confirm the diagnosis of diabetes mellitus? [1] b) What is the pathophysiology in type 1 and type 2 diabetes? [2] c) How do you manage an overweight recently diagnosed diabetic? [3] d) List two indications to start insulin in a diabetic? [2] e) How do you treat hypoglycemia in adults and neonate in a hospital setting? [2]

A 28-year-old returned from Chennai when he presented with high grade fever, with chills and rigors: a) What are the differential diagnosis of fever with chills and rigors? [2] b) What is severe complicated malaria? [3] c) Write briefly about management of acute uncomplicated malaria and severe falciparum malaria. [3] d) Mention drug schedule for Chemoprophylaxis in chloroquine sensitive and resistant areas. [2] 2024 May paper 1

A 40-year-old gentleman Mr. X presents to the family physician for routine check-up. On examination, his blood pressure was found to be 180/100 mmHg. He is reporting headache in the evenings for the past 1 month. He smokes 20 cigarettes per day for past 20 years. He consumes alcohol 180 ml per day for the past 5 years. His own brother had heart attack and angioplasty at the age of 40 years and he is worried whether he needs to take medications to prevent heart attack. a) What are the precautions you will take to avoid error in the measurement of blood pressure in your clinic? [1] b) How will you manage Mr. X? [4] c) Mention any three important anti-hypertensive drug classes recommended for Mr. X and mention their side effects. [3] d) What is hypertensive urgency and hypertensive emergency? [2]

A 35-year-old male presents with complaints of vomiting blood for the past 2 days. On examination, he is pale with pulse rate of 110/minute and blood pressure of 90/50 mmHg. a) What is the immediate management recommended? [4] b) What are the possible differential diagnosis causing blood vomiting? [1] c) What are the types of blood and blood products available for transfusion? [2] d) What are the reactions caused by blood transfusion and how will you manage the transfusion reaction? [3]

A 20-year-old male, a college dropout, presents to the casualty with alleged history of taking a large number of Tab. Paracetamol less than an hour ago with the intention of deliberate self-harm. He is conscious and oriented with normal vitals. a) Mention the principles in the immediate management a patient with any drug overdose. [4] b) How will you manage this person in the hospital and after discharge? [6]

A 40 year old obese lady with diabetes on your follow-up has presented with high grade fever and chills associated with vomiting and loin pain on right loin for past 1 day. On examination, she is febrile, toxic, dehydrated and has right renal angle tenderness. Her investigations showed urine WBC - 250 cells/cumm. a) How will you manage her in the first two days? [5] b) If the urine culture shows E.coli significant growth > 105 colonies grown, resistant to Cephalosporin and Penicillin group antibiotic, what is the preferred antibiotic of choice and justify your choice. [3] c) How will you manage this lady if this condition is recurring again? [2]

A 20-year-old lady, a college student, presents with the complains of multiple painful papules with central blackish keratotic material and surrounding erythema, present in her face, neck, chest and upper back. These lesions started two months back and recently some lesions are painful. She is very much worried and disturbed. a) What is the probable diagnosis? [2] b) What is the etiology and pathogenesis of this condition? [3] c) How will you manage this skin lesions? [3] d) What is the prognosis and when will you refer this lady to the specialist? [2]

A 45-year-old gentleman, a known case of hypertension on Tab. Amlodipine 10 mg once daily has come for follow-up. He is on regular medications and his blood pressure is 160/90 mm Hg. His BMI is 29 kg/ m2. His annual blood check-up shows Total Cholesterol - 280 mg/dl, Triglycerides - 155 mg/dl, HDL - 33 mg/dl and LDL cholesterol - 182 mg/dl. HbA1c - 7.8 %. His creatinine is 0.9 mg% and his urinary microalbumin excretion is 900 mg in 24 hours. a) Describe the pharmacological and non-pharmacological management needed for this patient. [5] b) Describe briefly the different oral anti-diabetic medications available – classification, mechanism of action and their side effects. [5]

A 65-year-old gentleman on treatment for hypertension with tab. Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once daily, presents to the casualty with altered sensorium. There was no h/o fever / vomiting / diarrhea. The blood work-up showed Random Blood sugar of 210 mg, Creatinine of 0.9 mg and Serum Sodium of 115 mEq/L and Potassium of 4 mEq/L a) What is the likely cause for his altered sensorium? [2] b) How will you manage this patient? [4] c) How will you prevent this happening in the future? [2] d) What are the indications for referral to the specialist? [2] 2025 June paper 1

A 45-year-old businessman comes to see you in the OPD with complaints of increasing abdominal distension. He consumes alcohol 180 to 360 ml daily for the past 10 years. On examination, you demonstrate fluid in the abdomen. a) What are the causes for ascites? [2] b) What are the other clinical features you will look for in this patient? [2] c) How will you further evaluate this person with ascites? [2] d) What are the complications of ascites? [2] e) How will you manage and follow up this person? [2]

A group of 4 people presented with multiple episodes of loose stools and vomiting after having food in a fast food restaurant. After assessing them, you decide to admit to correct dehydration and for further evaluation. a) What are the different causes of gastroenteritis? [2] b) What are the clinical features you would look for in these people? [2] c) How will you further evaluate and manage? [4] d) What are the complications of severe AGE and when will you refer? [2]

A 45-year-old man is on treatment for Parkinsonism and has come to see you for follow up. a) What is the aetiology for Parkinsonism? [2] b) What are the clinical features in Parkinsonism? [2] c) What are the differential diagnoses? [2] d) How will you treat and when would you refer? [4] 2025 June paper 1

A-78-year old lady with right sided hemiplegia is being discharged from hospital. Relatives are taking her to her home at a remote village. She is bedridden and is on indwelling catheter and Ryle’s tube feeding: a) What are the problems that you can anticipate in this patient? [2] b) What advice will you give to prevent bed sores in this patient? [3] c) How will you classify bedsores? [3] d) Family physician’s role in managing bed sores. [2]

A 40 year old lady came with dilated and tortuous veins over lower portion of her left leg. Discuss the following: a) Anatomy of venous system of lower limb. [3] b) Clinical features of varicose vein. [3] c) Prevention and management of varicose vein. [4]
Describe the anatomy, clinical features and management of plantar fasciitis. How can plantar fasciitis be prevented? [(3+3)+4]

What is the pathogenesis of osteo-arthritis (OA)? What are the common joints involved, their symptoms, clinical features of osteo-arthritis? Outline the relevant investigations and management of OA. [2+4+4]

A 10-year-old girl presented with purulent right ear discharge for last 3 days. She had similar complaints in the past on the same side. Describe in detail about clinical features, examination findings, investigations, treatment and complications of this condition. [2+2+2+2+2]
Describe briefly the clinical anatomy, indications, contra-indications and complications of ankle block. How will you do the procedure? [8+2]
Describe the possible ophthalmic complications of diabetes. Explain about stages of diabetic retinopathy and its management options available to the ophthalmologist. [5+(3+2)]

A 70 years old female, diabetic, strict vegetarian who is a mother of 5 children presented with history of dribbling of urine: a) Mention the types of urinary incontinence. [3] b) What are the possible aetiological factors in the case scenario given above? [3]

A 30 years old male presented with severe epigastric pain since one day. His PR-110 bpm, BP-100/60 mm hg, RR-25/min. Write 4 diagnostic possibilities you would consider in this patient. Describe in detail about clinical features, investigations and management of each. [4+6]
A 40 years old lady came with a 3 cm size lump in the left breast. Enumerate differential diagnosis and management of each. [4+6]

A 23-year-old Mrs. Renuka is being posted for emergency section for failed induction. a) Explain the clinical anatomy for spinal anesthesia with a diagram. [3] b) Discuss the pharmacological features of Bupivacaine used for spinal anesthesia. [3] c) What are the indications, contraindications, and complications of spinal anesthesia? [4]

A 35-year-old lady accidentally suffered burns over the upper thighs upto the knee joints on both sides and below the umbilicus on the anterior surface of the abdomen. a) How will you assess burns in an adult? [2] b) How will you monitor the patient for complications? [3] c) Discuss the burns management of this lady. [5]

A 51-year-old female presents with palpable swelling in her left breast of 3 months duration. She is post-menopausal for three years. She has no medical comorbidities. Menarche was at 11 years of age. She has 2 children with her first pregnancy at 29 years of age. a) How will you investigate this patient? [2] b) What are the current recommendations for screening for breast cancer? [3] c) Discuss the possible risk factors associated with malignancy of breast. [2] d) Outline the long term management of this patient by you as her family doctor. [3]

Mrs. Varalakshmi had a fall in the bathroom and is unable to move her right leg and not able to bear weight. She has tenderness over the right leg anterior aspect. a) Describe the principles in management of fractures with a special mention about fracture of the lower limbs. [6] b) What are the early and late complications? [4]

Mrs. Satya aged 40 years, presented to outpatient department with history of tiredness and fatigue, she gives history of heavy menstrual bleeding for 5 days, and on examination she is pale. a) What are the indications of blood transfusion? [2] b) What are the risks and complications of blood transfusion? [3] c) What tests will you do on the donor blood before transfusion? [2] d) What measures will you take before, during and after the transfusion in the ward? [3]

A 18-year-old married lady, presents with pain in the right side of the abdomen for the past one day. On examination, she has tenderness in the right iliac fossa. a) What is your differential diagnosis? [3] b) What relevant history and examination will you perform? [3] c) How will you manage this condition if the patient is in shock? [4]

A 15-year-old Sridhar presented to your OPD with history of profuse right ear discharge for 6 weeks? a) What is your diagnosis? What are the salient features? [2] b) What are the risk factors? Mention four common pathogens causing this condition? [3] c) What are the complications of this condition? [3] d) How will you manage this condition? [2]

A 35-year-old Devi, an agricultural worker, mother of two children, has come to the out- patient clinic with history of pain and discharge from Right eye associated with blurring of vision since she returned from the field. The right eye is red, and the cornea has haziness. a) List any THREE possible differential diagnosis. [3] b) How will you manage Mrs. Devi, if she refuses referral to eye doctor in the next town, as she need to take care of the two children? [7]

A 56-year-old postman comes with pain in the legs for the last 3 years. Pain occurs in both the thighs and legs after walking for 15 min. It is relieved by rest. Since last two months, he has pain when he walks a short distance. He has been smoking about 6 to 8 cigarettes per day for the past 20 years. He also hurt his right leg over the lateral aspect few weeks ago and the wound is not healing: a) What is the probable diagnosis and differential diagnosis? [1] b) What clinical features would you look for? [2] c) How will you investigate this patient? [2] d) What treatment will you offer for the condition as well as the ulcer? [2] e) How will you help him to stop smoking? [3]
A 66-year-old lady presented with painful swelling of the lower eyelid near the bridge of the nose: a) Enumerate the differential diagnosis. [3] b) Discuss the management. [7]

You are called to see a lady who was injured by a stove burst: a) What first aid will you provide? [2] b) How will you assess the severity of different injuries that the patient may suffer? [5] c) How will you manage this patient after discharge from the hospital? [3]

A 35-year-old labourer has come with low back which started suddenly after he lifted a heavy object: a) List the red flags in a patient presenting with low backache. [2] b) Discuss the history and clinical features of lumbosacral intervertebral disc prolapse, including a note on the dermatomes of the lower limb. [4] c) How will you assess if a patient with lumbosacral disc prolapse needs urgent referral? [2] d) Outline conservative management of lumbosacral disc prolapse. [2]
A 14-year-old old boy presents with fever and sore throat: a) Write the differential diagnosis. [5] b) Discuss rational use of antibiotics for treating patients with sore throat. [5]

A 24-year-old lady presents with a swelling in the right breast. Swelling is freely mobile and on palpation of the left breast, the physician detects two small swellings. Her grandmother died of carcinoma of breast and her mother is being treated for the same. Patient is worried about her conditon: a) What is the probable diagnosis? [1] b) What investigations will you do? [2] c) When will you refer the patient to a surgeon? [2] d) She wants to undergo special investigations she read about in the internet to screen for cancer. What will you advise her? [2] e) She has a 1-year-old child and wanted to discuss about contraception. What would you advise her? [3]

A 48-year-old farmer who has been a diabetic for the last 15 years and on oral anti- diabetic drugs and insulin presents with an ulcer on the plantar aspect of the left foot: a) Describe physical examination findings that can help you in the assessment and management of the ulcer. [3] b) How wiill you manage the ulcer in family practice? [3] c) Discuss indications for referral to a surgeon. [2] d) Write a note on prevention of diabetic foot ulcer. [2]

A 28-year-old married lady presents to a remote community health centre with fever and acute abdominal pain for the past 3 days. Pain is localised to the right illiac fossa. She has missed her periods by 5 days. On examination, she has tenderness in the right iliac fossa with no guarding or rigidity: a) What is the differential diagnosis for this presentation and the most probable cause? [2] b) How will you investigate her? [3] c) Can this patient be treated in a community health centre? If so, what is the treatment that you will recommend? [3] d) What are the indications for referral to a higher centre? [2]
A labourer comes with severe pain in the right hand with a high fever. On examination, the right palm is swollen with tenderness over the mid palmar area:

A male patient who has sex with men comes with severe pain and bleeding form the anal region: a) What is the differential diagnosis? [3] b) What investigations will you order? Give the reasons for the same. [4] c) What treatment will you provide for infective causes for this presentation? [3]

A 42-year-old man has been diagnosed with diabetes for the last 5 years. He has been coming to you for regular follow up: a) How will you perform his foot examination?
